subject: DPA: training prohibition, subprocessor list & SCCs — redlines and execution
messages:
From: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@luminahealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@luminahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines — strict non-training carve-out + subprocessor list

Hi Sean,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. This is moving quickly on our side; procurement and security reviewed and we have a couple of non-negotiable asks before we can sign:

- Explicit prohibition on using Lumina Health customer data for model training, tuning, or algorithmic improvements (we need the exact language to prevent "derivative" or "improvement" uses).
- If any telemetry or logs are used for service improvement, it must be aggregated, fully de-identified, and only after a 90-day delay; we need details on what data elements are retained.
- Complete subprocessor list (current + prospective) and an obligation to notify us 30 days before adding EU/EMEA-based subprocessors.
- Cross-border transfers: we require SCCs (standard contractual clauses) and details on where backups are stored.

I've attached our redlines (Lumina_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx) — the key issues are on pages 3 and 7. Please confirm whether Redwood will accept the non-training carve-out as written or propose alternate language. We also need an audit-obligations bullet so our InfoSec team can sign off.

We'd like to get this wrapped up by end of week; procurement is standing by to execute once legal signs off.

Thanks,
Ellen Marsh
Head of Security & Privacy
Lumina Health

---
Attachment: Lumina_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx (docx)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@luminahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — strict non-training carve-out + subprocessor list

Ellen — thanks for the clear callouts and the redlines doc. I'm looping in Marissa (Legal) and Neha (Security/compliance) so we can respond with position and proposed language.

Quick high-level: Redwood's position is to prohibit customer data from being used to train or fine-tune general-purpose models unless the customer provides explicit opt-in. We do use aggregated telemetry for product quality improvements (e.g., latency, error rates); we can commit to your 90-day delay and de-identification requirement in principle, but we need to align on definitions (what "de-identified" means operationally).

Marissa/Neha — can you review Ellen's redlines and propose exact counter-language we can share today? Also confirm whether we can produce a current subprocessor list and provide 30-day notification for EU subprocessors.

I'll schedule a 30-minute call for tomorrow to walk through the sensitive items unless you'd prefer to continue in thread.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@luminahealth.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 14:08:10 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — strict non-training carve-out + subprocessor list

Ellen — thanks for the detailed redlines. We've reviewed internally (legal + applied ML). Below are our proposed positions; please let us know which points are deal-breakers for Lumina so we can prioritize: 

1) Training prohibition — proposed compromise language:
   "Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve any models that are made generally available outside the Customer environment, except with Customer's prior, express, written consent."
   Rationale: this preserves Lumina's prohibition while allowing explicit opt-in for narrow use cases.

2) "Derivative" outputs — we propose adding: "The definition of Customer Data does not include outputs that are solely generated by Redwood models in response to Customer requests; however, any such outputs that are retained by Redwood and used for model improvements shall be subject to the prohibition above unless consented to."

3) Aggregation & de-identification — we can accept aggregation + 90-day delay for telemetry limited to service metrics. We need a mutually acceptable definition of "de-identified"; we propose the ISO/IEC 20889 reference combined with a ban on persistent user identifiers.

4) Subprocessor list & notice — we will provide the current subprocessor list within 48 hours and accept a 30-day notification obligation before adding EU-based subprocessors. We will not require prior approval for routine updates, but will give Lumina the option to review and object for material security/regulatory reasons.

5) SCCs & backups — Redwood will execute SCCs for EU transfers and provide a summary of backup locations and retention policy. If Lumina requires bespoke transfer measures, we can surface that as a commercial-term escalation.

6) Audit rights — we can offer: (a) annual third-party SOC 2 Type II report access; (b) reasonable on-site or remote audit rights limited to once per year with notice. For deeper audits, we propose a separate scope/cost discussion.

Please see the attached Redlines_summary_for_Redwood.pdf for redline snippets and suggested DocuSign text. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow at 11am PT.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redlines_summary_for_Redwood.pdf (pdf)

From: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@luminahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@luminahealth.com>, procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 08:34:55 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — strict non-training carve-out + subprocessor list

Marissa — thanks for the quick and thorough reply. Lumina can accept the compromise language in (1) provided that: 

- The definition of "Customer Data" explicitly includes any data submitted via API and any PII derived from it.
- The opt-in path cannot be implied; it must be a separate signed addendum per product instance.

On (2) and (3): we appreciate the ISO reference and the 90-day delay. We want a short example list of the telemetry fields Redwood considers "service metrics" so our InfoSec can confirm no re-identification risk.

Subprocessors: we reviewed the current list your team shared — a few prospective vendors are fine, but we need 30-day notice for any subcontractor that has access to unredacted Customer Data.

Audit: SOC 2 access is fine; we will accept the once-per-year remote audit with 30 days' notice.

Attached is a redline that integrates Marissa's language with minor clarifications. If Redwood is happy with these points, procurement will sign via DocuSign — we have a blank DocuSign envelope ready.

Looking forward to the 11am PT call.

Best,
Ellen

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Ellen Marsh <ellen.marsh@luminahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — strict non-training carve-out + subprocessor list

Ellen — great to close this out. Post-call we incorporated your modest clarifications into the final DPA and have accepted the following in the execution copy:

- Explicit non-training clause matching the compromise (opt-in must be written and signed as an addendum).
- Customer Data defined to include API-submitted data and derived PII.
- Aggregated telemetry limited to service-level metrics; Redwood will provide a short field list (see link below) and commits to a 90-day aging period and removal of persistent identifiers.
- Current subprocessor list shared and Redwood will provide 30-day notice for additions that could access unredacted Customer Data. Routine operational subprocessor changes will be notified but not require prior approval.

I've sent a DocuSign envelope to procurement (link below). Please have procurement execute the envelope; if Lumina prefers to send the envelope we can sign the other side.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/LUM-2027-042
Telemetry fields summary: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cSamples

Thanks for the pragmatic approach. We'll treat this as the standard template for regulated healthcare customers going forward and share a short internal note.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
